hints: Cumulative frequencies must be plotted at the upper class boundaries: (15, 18), (25, 46), (30, 88), (40, 140), (50, 176), (70, 200).
Include a plausible starting point at cumulative frequency 0, such as (0, 0) or (5, 0).
Label both axes: horizontal axis 'Time (minutes)' and vertical axis 'Cumulative frequency'.
Join the points with a smooth increasing curve or straight line segments.
walkthrough:
Plot the cumulative frequency points at the upper class boundaries on linear scales:
$$(15, 18), \quad (25, 46), \quad (30, 88), \quad (40, 140), \quad (50, 176), \quad (70, 200)$$

Connect the plotted points with an increasing curve or polygon starting from the horizontal axis (at $t = 0$ or $(0, 0)$):
- Horizontal axis: labelled 'Time ($t$ minutes)' from $0$ to $70$.
- Vertical axis: labelled 'Cumulative frequency' from $0$ to $200$.

ai_rubric.Constructing Cumulative Frequency Graphs: Plots points at upper boundaries with appropriate linear scales and labels.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand where cumulative frequencies are plotted:
Cumulative frequency represents the total number of observations up to a given threshold.
Therefore, each cumulative frequency must be plotted at the upper boundary of the corresponding interval:
- $t = 15 \implies \text{cf} = 18$
- $t = 25 \implies \text{cf} = 46$
- $t = 30 \implies \text{cf} = 88$
- $t = 40 \implies \text{cf} = 140$
- $t = 50 \implies \text{cf} = 176$
- $t = 70 \implies \text{cf} = 200$

Step 2: Plot the points on linear axes:
- Horizontal axis: Time $t$ in minutes ($0$ to $70$).
- Vertical axis: Cumulative frequency ($0$ to $200$).

Step 3: Draw the curve:
Start from the baseline $(0, 0)$ and join the plotted points with a smooth, continuously non-decreasing curve or straight-line segments.

hints: For total frequency N = 200, find the positions on the vertical axis:
Median position is 0.5 * 200 = 100. Read the corresponding time from your graph (expected between 31 and 33 minutes).
Lower quartile Q1 position is 0.25 * 200 = 50 (expected between 25 and 27 minutes).
Upper quartile Q3 position is 0.75 * 200 = 150 (expected between 42 and 44 minutes).
Calculate IQR = Q3 - Q1 (expected between 15 and 19 minutes).
walkthrough:
Read the median from the cumulative frequency graph at $\text{cf} = 0.5 \times 200 = 100$:
$$\text{Median} \approx 32\text{ minutes} \quad (31 \le \text{Median} \le 33)$$

Read the lower and upper quartiles from the graph:
- Lower quartile $Q_1$ at $\text{cf} = 0.25 \times 200 = 50$:
$$Q_1 \approx 26\text{ minutes} \quad (25 \le Q_1 \le 27)$$
- Upper quartile $Q_3$ at $\text{cf} = 0.75 \times 200 = 150$:
$$Q_3 \approx 43\text{ minutes} \quad (42 \le Q_3 \le 44)$$

Calculate the interquartile range (IQR):
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 \approx 43 - 26 = 17\text{ minutes} \quad (15 \le \text{IQR} \le 19)$$

ai_rubric.Finding Medians and Quartiles: Reads the median and quartiles at cf = 100, 50, and 150 from the graph.
ai_rubric.Calculating the Interquartile Range: Finds the difference between the upper and lower quartiles.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the cumulative frequency levels for the summary statistics:
For total pupils $N = 200$:
- Median position: $0.5 \times 200 = 100$
- Lower quartile ($Q_1$) position: $0.25 \times 200 = 50$
- Upper quartile ($Q_3$) position: $0.75 \times 200 = 150$

Step 2: Read values from the cumulative frequency curve:
- At cumulative frequency $100$: trace horizontally to the curve and vertically down to read the time:
$$\text{Median} \approx 32\text{ minutes} \quad (31 \le \text{median} \le 33)$$
- At cumulative frequency $50$:
$$Q_1 \approx 26\text{ minutes} \quad (25 \le Q_1 \le 27)$$
- At cumulative frequency $150$:
$$Q_3 \approx 43\text{ minutes} \quad (42 \le Q_3 \le 44)$$

Step 3: Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 43 - 26 = 17\text{ minutes} \quad (15 \le \text{IQR} \le 19)$$

skill_tags: Estimating Mean and Variance from Grouped Data
Calculating a Mean from Raw Data

hints: Find the class intervals, class frequencies f, and midpoints x from the cumulative frequency table:
Divide by total frequency 200: mean = 6730 / 200 = 33.65 minutes.
walkthrough:
Determine the individual class frequencies and interval midpoints from the cumulative frequencies:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Interval} & \text{Cumulative Frequency} & \text{Frequency } (f) & \text{Midpoint } (x) & f \times x \\
\hline
0 < t \le 15 & 18 & 18 & 7.5 & 135 \\
15 < t \le 25 & 46 & 46 - 18 = 28 & 20 & 560 \\
25 < t \le 30 & 88 & 88 - 46 = 42 & 27.5 & 1155 \\
30 < t \le 40 & 140 & 140 - 88 = 52 & 35 & 1820 \\
40 < t \le 50 & 176 & 176 - 140 = 36 & 45 & 1620 \\
50 < t \le 70 & 200 & 200 - 176 = 24 & 60 & 1440 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

Calculate the estimated mean using $\bar{t} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$:
$$\sum fx = 135 + 560 + 1155 + 1820 + 1620 + 1440 = 6730$$
$$\bar{t} = \frac{6730}{200} = 33.65\text{ minutes} \approx 33.7\text{ minutes}$$

ai_rubric.Estimating Mean and Variance from Groupe: Multiplies correct class frequencies by class midpoints and divides by total frequency.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Extract individual class frequencies from the cumulative frequency table:
- Interval $0 < t \le 15$: $f_1 = 18$
- Interval $15 < t \le 25$: $f_2 = 46 - 18 = 28$
- Interval $25 < t \le 30$: $f_3 = 88 - 46 = 42$
- Interval $30 < t \le 40$: $f_4 = 140 - 88 = 52$
- Interval $40 < t \le 50$: $f_5 = 176 - 140 = 36$
- Interval $50 < t \le 70$: $f_6 = 200 - 176 = 24$

Step 3: Compute the sum of the products fx:
$$\sum fx = (18 \times 7.5) + (28 \times 20) + (42 \times 27.5) + (52 \times 35) + (36 \times 45) + (24 \times 60)$$
$$\sum fx = 135 + 560 + 1155 + 1820 + 1620 + 1440 = 6730$$

Step 4: Divide by total frequency:
$$\bar{t} = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = \frac{6730}{200} = 33.65\text{ minutes}$$
(Accept $33.65$ or $33.7$ minutes).
